answer: For a proposed meadow nectar telemetry market using a copper bus, each listed ID reserves one certified chip. A registry checks vendor certificates and fresh ID-bound nonce signatures, enforcing one active ID per chip; failure denies or revokes listing. Chips are reusable capital; rentals recur; no stake. Honest one-certificate-per-chip issuance and protected keys are essential; signatures do not prove readings true, and cheap rentals weaken deterrence. Ten concurrent IDs need ten chips: shared hosts and parallel signing cannot multiply one certificate's listing.
